source.title: The Geometry of Refusal in Large Language Models: Concept Cones and Representational Independence
source.authors: Tom Wollschlager; Jannes Elstner; Simon Geisler; Vincent Cohen-Addad; Stephan Gunnemann; Johannes Gasteiger

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether refusal is mediated by a single direction and reports refusal cones and multiple independent refusal directions, refining the single-direction account. It does not test toy-model superposition or feature superposition generally.
record.gate_note: The cone-dimension, independent-direction, and compositional-ablation results bear on V6. RDO-versus-DIM attack performance, benchmark side effects, and refusal induction results are not included as rows unless they report a geometric or multi-directional finding. The reported feature and SAE literature is cited background, not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The study does not test superposition. It optimises refusal-mediating directions and cones in chat LLMs and measures jailbreak ASR under ablation. No version of the claim is tested. V6 asks whether superposed features are 1-D directions or irreducibly multi-dimensional. A cone of many directions that each mediate refusal under intervention is a different construct. It does not show that any feature is multi-dimensional, and it does not involve superposition, sparsity or capacity. The record's own V6 note concedes this. These results are therefore filed under fits_no_version, not given V6 verdicts.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that refusal is better described by multi-dimensional polyhedral cones than by a single direction. They find that orthogonality does not imply independence under intervention, and that several representationally independent refusal directions exist and correspond to distinct mechanisms. They also claim their gradient-based RDO yields refusal directions with fewer side effects than DIM.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses gradient-based Refusal Direction Optimization and Refusal Cone Optimization on chat LLMs, evaluating refusal interventions and ASR. It does not reproduce the original toy-network feature-superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Cone performance varies with cone dimensionality and model size; ASR gains plateau at four dimensions for Gemma 2 2B. In best-of-N comparisons, the cone advantage is reported in the low-sample regime, while randomness dominates at higher sample counts.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal in chat LLMs (Gemma 2, Qwen 2.5, Llama 3) is mediated by polyhedral cones of up to 5 dimensions and by several representationally independent directions. Ablating these directions together raises ASR additively. Larger Qwen models support higher-dimensional cones.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Behavioural concepts such as refusal are mediated by multi-dimensional regions or multiple independent directions rather than a single linear direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Orthogonal refusal directions are not independent under intervention: ablating one reduces the other's cosine representation in later layers (Fig 6, Fig 21).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Euclidean orthogonality of directions does not imply causal or representational independence in LLMs.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The geometric ASR results are largely presented in figures without numerical values in the text. The authors note that the independent directions are optimized on the same targets, which may limit how fully distinct the mechanisms are; they also cannot rule out other undiscovered refusal-mediating regions.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. RDO-versus-DIM results, benchmark side effects, activation-addition refusal scores, and adversarial suffix results were left out because they do not directly measure whether refusal is represented by one versus multiple directions or cones.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparse features, phase transition or geometry of superposed features.
No neuron polysemanticity or capacity competition.
No measure of features spread across neurons and no SAE/dictionary recovery.
No test of whether superposed features are 1-D or irreducibly multi-dimensional. Refusal cones are sets of intervention directions, not shown to be a single multi-dimensional feature.

missing.what: Orthogonal RDO⊥ vs DIM interaction under ablation (cosine similarity across layers), and the GCG suffix reducing RepInd-1 representation (36% ASR).
missing.locator: Section 6.1 Fig 6, Appendix F Fig 21; Section 6.2 Fig 9

record.verdict_notes: The paper never mentions superposition or Toy Models of Superposition. Its relevance to V6 is only by analogy (single vs multi-dimensional). The record's 'tests/T5' and its V6 challenges and limits_scope labels are overturned. ASR values for the cone and RepInd results are figure-only.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, sparse features, feature overlap, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry are not studied.
The study does not investigate neuron polysemanticity, feature competition for capacity, or dedicated versus shared dimensions.
The study does not investigate causes of polysemantic neurons other than capacity pressure.
It does not measure feature distribution across neurons or recover features with a dictionary or SAE.
The study does not evaluate whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.

It examines the geometry of refusal in chat LLMs, not whether features in superposition generally are individual multidimensional features. Its cones are sets of refusal-mediating directions, so it does not establish that any one feature is multidimensional.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 2B
rows.operation_detail: Compare best-of-N attacks sampled from a four-dimensional refusal cone with best-of-N attacks using the single-dimensional RDO direction and temperature sampling.
rows.baseline: Single-dimensional RDO direction with temperature sampling, using the same number of attacks
rows.value: Cone-direction sampling has higher ASR in the low-sample regime; plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: The authors interpret the low-sample result as evidence that different directions capture complementary aspects of refusal.
rows.check: Best-of-N comparison with selection per prompt. Not a measure of feature dimensionality. Advantage holds only in the low-sample regime; randomness dominates at higher N.

rows.subject: Gemma 2, Qwen 2.5, and Llama 3 models (figure aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measure directional-ablation ASR for iteratively found refusal directions that are representationally independent of DIM and previously found directions.
rows.value: The authors report that multiple independent directions have ASR significantly above random-vector intervention, with ASR declining as more directions are searched for; plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: The text reports the qualitative result across models but does not provide model-specific numerical values.
rows.check: Several RepInd directions beat the random-vector baseline, with ASR declining by rank. This bears on independent refusal mechanisms, not V6.

source_check.correct: Multiple representationally independent directions achieve ASR significantly above random-vector intervention; ASR declines with successive directions. State=cannot_determine; versions=none.
source_check.problem: Independent refusal mechanisms do not establish overlapping feature storage or irreducible feature dimensionality.

rows.note: The authors interpret the additive ASR gains as evidence that the directions capture different aspects of refusal.

relation.reason: Its discussion of linear concept representations and multidimensional refusal geometry is related context; its experiments do not test a listed version.

tranche.reason: The study tests refusal geometry and intervention independence, without testing or operationally using the catalog's superposition claims.

source_check.notes: Multiple refusal-mediating directions do not establish an irreducibly multidimensional superposed feature. Qualitative row values are supported by prose; numerical ASRs cannot be recovered from the figure-only text.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Tested chat LLMs and refusal behavior
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports multi-dimensional refusal cones and multiple independent refusal directions rather than a single refusal direction (r1, r4, r5, r6). This challenges a single-direction account for refusal, but does not show that individual superposed features are themselves multidimensional.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The multidirectional effects are bounded: Gemma 2 2B cone ASR plateaus at four dimensions, and Qwen 2.5 cone lower bounds degrade with increasing dimension, with larger models appearing to support higher-dimensional cones (r2, r4).
